newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan likely to cut 97/98 spending -opposition.
newsitem.headline: Japan likely to cut 97/98 spending -opposition.

text.p: Japan's major political parties are likely to agree on slashing next fiscal year's state spendings by a few trillion yen, Naoto Kan, leader of the opposition Democratic Party, told reporters on Monday.
"I think we will be able to agree on few trillions of yen worth of reductions," said Kan, a key campaigner for a slimmer government and reduced spending.

Kan's party is asking the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and two others in loose alliance with the LDP to cut the spending in the full state budget for the fiscal year from April 1997, by over three trillion yen.
The Democratic Party, a smaller opposition party, is asking the reduction to be be made especially in public works projects.
It has also called for scrapping rules which mandate the use of certain tax revenues for designated purposes. The parties will meet again on Friday to discuss the issue.
Asked whether the cut will be made in the original state budget or through a supplementary budget, Kan said that the party was asking for revisions in the original budget.
Japan's parliament is currently debating the state budget for 1997/98 worth 77.39 trillion yen.
"It won't be easy," Kan said. "But if we are able to achieve what we set out to do, this will be a big step forward in reforms."
He added that the ruling parties' response on state spending will be one of the major factors in deciding whether the party will side with the LDP when voting on the budget.
Kan said that siding with the LDP on the budget did not necessarily mean that the Democratic Party was joining the ruling alliance.
He said the party will consider all options in what he termed fighting with the bureaucrats to push through reforms.
